column1: # Local corrections to the word list (An Gramadóir 0.70 lexicon, data/lexicon.json).
# Built into data/lexicon-corrections.json by tools/build-data.mjs and applied when the
# checker loads, after the BuNaMo overlay (src/lexicon.ts). Our own work, under
# the project's licence; kept apart from the BuNaMo overlay, which is ODbL.
# One word per line, tab-separated: the word, its tags (as in ga/pos-ga.txt,
# written one after another), and the reason. The tags replace all the word's
# tags; the word keeps its frequency tier. A word not in the word list is added
# to it (in the rarest tier). If it is in the table of non-standard forms
# (data/eile.json), the correction says it is standard, so it is removed from
# that table. Otherwise it is a new word, and its reason must start with the
# source that gives it (focloir.ie, FGB or CO17, or Liam (date) for his own decision), or the build stops. Lines
# Tags written =form mark a spelling the standard does not use, with form as the
# correction (several separated by ", "). A word in the
# word list is taken out of it; a word in the non-standard table gets this
# correction in place of the table's; any other word needs a cited source.
# Reference: CO17 = Gramadach na Gaeilge: An Caighdeán Oifigiúil, 2017.
# A preposition or conjunction fused with the copula (CO17 7.3.2, 7.3.3, Táblaí
# 7O-7R). The word list has most of these as the copula (inarb, lenarb, darb,
# faoinarbh, sularbh, ...) but these only as rare words, so they were reported
# as rare, and the word after them as needing the copula (ónarb áil, sularb eol).

CO17 Tábla 5T: go bhfeice tú (the subjunctive of feic); both mutated forms, as the table has faca: bhfaca, fhaca. The table gave feac (FGB feac1: Var f, gs. feice, spade), a far rarer word than the verb.
CO17 Tábla 5X: chuaigh mé (the past of téigh is lenited). Without this a spelling rule read it as cuach.
teanglann (grammar database) daingniú: gs. and pl. daingnithe; FGB daingniú1 gives daingniúchán as a variant (Var: ~chán m), of which this is the gs. and pl. The table gave the headword daingniú.
